title: Baking sunflower hulls within an aluminum envelope in a common laboratory oven yields charcoal
author: Arnal

steps.title: Obtain sunflower hulls
steps.instruction: Extract multi‑layered hulls (pericarps) from sunflower achenes.

substeps.instruction: Press each sunflower achene with tongue‑and‑groove pliers along its major axis until it cracks.
Peel the cracked achenes by hand.
Discard the seeds and collect the multi‑layered hulls.

steps.title: Prepare aluminum envelope
steps.instruction: Pack 1 g of hulls into an airtight aluminum foil envelope.

substeps.instruction: Cut two squares of aluminum foil, each approximately 28 cm × 28 cm, from a commercial roll.
Lay one foil square on a larger sheet of paper on the bench (paper protects the foil from being cut).
Fold the foil by joining two opposite sides, keeping the matte side inside and the shiny side outside; press the fold with a finger while moving from one end to the other, then unfold.
Place exactly 1 g of sunflower hulls at the centre of the unfolded foil and refold so the hulls remain inside the rectangle formed by the bend.
Seal the longest open side:
a. Mark a line 5 mm from the border of the longest side with a ruler.
b. Bend the 5‑mm‑high strip 180° and press with a finger from one extreme to the other.
c. Repeat steps a–b twice, taking care not to cut the foil with the hulls inside.
d. Press the foil from the outside to expel as much air as possible.
Seal the two shorter sides using the same 5‑mm‑line folding procedure.
Wrap the sealed envelope with the second 28 cm × 28 cm foil piece, sealing its longest and shorter sides as described above.

steps.title: Thermal treatment in oven
steps.instruction: Heat the sealed envelope in a laboratory oven following a controlled program.

substeps.instruction: Place the aluminum envelope containing the hulls in the oven.
Start the heating program: ramp temperature at 10 °C min⁻¹ up to a final temperature (Tfinal) between 150 °C and 500 °C, testing at 50 °C intervals.
Hold the sample at Tfinal for 2 h.
Ensure the metallic envelope does not contact or short‑circuit the oven heating elements.
When the program ends, turn the oven off before opening.
Using crucible tongs, goggles, and insulating gloves, remove the hot envelope (it cools quickly but may still burn).

steps.title: Open envelope and collect carbon
steps.instruction: Retrieve the carbonized hulls from the cooled envelope.

substeps.instruction: Gently tap the envelope against the bench to let the solid fall inside the envelope.
Cut the upper side of the envelope with scissors.
Work in a fume hood or outdoors because smelly gaseous products are released during heating.
Transfer the solid carbon product to a storage flask.
